summary: Status unchanged since the last report. Completed: QC on all 12 WS2 spectra; single-spectrum fits at 578.95 nm and 638.38 nm. Pending: the 12-spectrum series fit, relaunched as background task b1tgx57b9 with a 2-hour limit; no output yet. Stopped: the earlier series run bn3z3cra8, killed at its 10-minute limit with no output. Key results: 2LA(M) at 352.7 and E2g1 at 358.5 cm-1 are resolved at 578.95 nm and absent at 638.38 nm; Si-corrected A1g is about 417.9 to 418.0 cm-1 in both spectra; the Si line drifts by about 1.1 cm-1 across the series, which is a calibration signature.

observations.finding: 2LA(M) and E2g1 are resolved at 578.95 nm and absent at 638.38 nm.
Si-corrected A1g is about 417.9 to 418.0 cm-1 in both spectra; the raw difference is calibration.
The Si line drifts monotonically with excitation wavelength, indicating a calibration change.

caveats: The 12-spectrum series (b1tgx57b9) has not reported; no series trend is given.
The 578.95 nm fit includes unconstrained broad components (532, 566 cm-1) that are likely background, so the 2LA/E2g1 positions may shift with a different background model.
Resonance interpretation rests on two spectra; the exciton energy is unknown.
Si drift is a calibration signature, not sample physics.
questions_for_user: Can you provide the flake's exciton energy at 4 K (PL or reflectance)? It decides whether 638 nm is below the A exciton.
Was the spectrometer recalibrated between wavelengths? The Si drift is about 1.1 cm-1.
